steps.message:
# Merge duplicate billing tickets

The support desk runs its tickets in the `tickets` service, which you can use through the `tickets` MCP server.

Some open tickets of the billing team are duplicates. Two open billing tickets are duplicates when they have the same customer and name the same order: the order number is on the line that starts with `Order:` in the ticket body.

For every group of duplicates:

1. Keep the ticket with the lowest id open and unchanged.
2. Set every other ticket of the group to status `duplicate`.
3. Add exactly one comment to each ticket you set to `duplicate`, with the text `Duplicate of #<id>`, where `<id>` is the id of the ticket that stays open.

Only open tickets of the billing team count. Do not change, comment on or create any other ticket.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.
I'll start by discovering the tickets MCP tools.

arguments.query: list tickets, update ticket status, add comment

steps.message:
I merged the duplicate billing tickets and wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`. I didn't re-query the tickets afterwards. Each update call returned `status: duplicate` and each comment call returned a comment id.

I read all 29 open billing tickets and found six groups with the same customer and order number. In each group the lowest id stays open and unchanged. Every other ticket in the group got one comment and was set to `duplicate`.

| Customer | Order | Kept open | Set to duplicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| olga.mora@example.com | ORD-45756 | #101 | #118, #122 |
| pablo.fuentes@example.com | ORD-43901 | #103 | #123 |
| jorge.reyes@example.com | ORD-48544 | #105 | #112, #120 |
| irene.pinto@example.com | ORD-44451 | #108 | #111 |
| elena.pinto@example.com | ORD-46825 | #117 | #124 |
| olga.fuentes@example.com | ORD-44866 | #127 | #128 |

Each comment reads `Duplicate of #<kept id>`, using the id from the table. I left every other ticket untouched.

I matched on customer and order number only, so some pairs have different titles (for example #108 and #111). Ticket #129 is also jorge.reyes@example.com but names a different order (ORD-55473), so it stays open.
